claims.statement: MCP configuration interpolates only `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` in command, URL, argument, environment, header, and OAuth fields; malformed references or an unset required variable are rejected before the resolved configuration is used.

MCP disabled-server names are unioned from user and managed policy and filtered before server validation or connection; an unreadable or invalid managed deny list fails closed by disabling every candidate server.

Workspace bindings persist a bounded allowlisted snapshot of reportable policy values, and refusal diagnostics expose only safe field changes or an unavailable marker; paths, credentials, environment values, model data, and prompts are excluded from diagnostic persistence and logging.

The configuration resolver orders managed policy, CLI, reload overrides, environment, user TOML, and defaults by ascending numeric rank; replacement options select the strongest usable value, while union and deep-merge options retain contributions from all valid tiers and record provenance.

The shared resolver builds its provider chain from keyword-only managed and user snapshots, caches one generation for normal process reads, and rejects installing a different CLI provider in the same process.

Managed-policy refresh candidates are fetched before resolver replacement and cannot replace the active managed tier unless they serve a usable policy snapshot, preventing a broken refresh from dropping restrictions to weaker tiers.

Project dotenv loading derives an explicit environment snapshot in which inherited values win and dotenv files only fill absent keys; project dotenv files are denied security-sensitive keys such as MCP trust lists, Auto classifier settings, recursion fallback, and terminal tracing metadata.

ServerConfig is the typed client-to-server configuration schema: it serializes configuration to prefixed environment variables with None clearing a variable, reconstructs it in the server process, and rejects malformed or unsafe filesystem-tool allowlists rather than treating them as unrestricted access.

A workspace binding canonicalizes an existing workspace directory, persists server-resolved non-secret policy and separate policy/runtime fingerprints in SQLite, atomically rejects a different workspace or incompatible policy, and permits a compatible runtime identity change to rebuild without discarding the binding.

Project-scoped MCP, sandbox setup, and extension policy is retained only for the launch project; another or unresolvable project drops those grants and re-evaluates extension trust, while execution rejects bound policy drift and treats runtime-only identity changes as a rebuild condition.

Each server runtime is built with an immutable workspace dotenv and credential snapshot, and all workspaces sharing a server must have matching LangSmith tracing selectors and redaction setting because tracing uses process-wide SDK state.
When LangSmith secret redaction is requested for an active upload target, failure to install the redacting client disables tracing rather than allowing unredacted uploads.

User `config.toml` updates are serialized, reject writes to the managed path and malformed existing TOML, replace the target atomically, and only best-effort refresh the shared resolver after the write has committed.

The configuration manifest defines option types, defaults, TOML locations, and environment-variable names; malformed scalar environment or TOML values are treated as invalid and resolution falls through without discarding valid sibling settings, while secret-bearing structured tables are redacted in introspection.
A `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_`-prefixed environment variable takes precedence over its canonical name even when empty, allowing an empty prefixed variable to suppress a canonical credential or setting.

The shared resolver serves a cached generation for normal process readers until a reload or default-path configuration write advances it, while the environment provider reads the live process environment or a context-local immutable snapshot at resolution time.

Managed configuration resolves from fixed operating-system paths, and Windows production lookup reads ProgramData from HKLM rather than a user-controlled environment variable; a registry fallback is marked indeterminate so an uncertain path is not mistaken for absent policy.
A durable configuration result masks only lower-priority non-durable results for replacement options, while an invalid durable tier falls through and remains represented in ranked health diagnostics.

A TOML provider retains its last usable snapshot after a failed reload, whereas an initial unreadable or corrupt snapshot contributes no values and resolution falls through to defaults or weaker tiers.
Project dotenv interpolation is evaluated against the original environment baseline, preventing project dotenv values from influencing interpolation performed by the trusted global dotenv.

Before spawning the agent server, `start_server_and_get_agent()` validates an explicit `--mcp-config` unless MCP is disabled; it turns missing-file and ordinary configuration validation failures into actionable `MCPConfigError` messages while leaving unrelated runtime failures unmasked.

The server manager preflights explicit MCP configuration, serializes a path-normalized `ServerConfig` before spawning the server, and requires a workspace before assigning the remote agent its session-only policy claim and session-claim fingerprint.
